scope: Official FX-Clover blog text for posts 8268, 7691, 6979, 7022, 7891 and 8090, plus official YouTube description metadata where explicitly noted. No unavailable video detail is inferred.

sources.title: FX ずらした移動平均線DMA【ポコニカル活用エントリーと決済について】

claims.claim: The official blog/video description explicitly teaches shifted DMA as a tool for Poconical entry and exit, including comparing the MA before and after displacement and explaining the author's DiNapoli-DMA interpretation.

The author explicitly attributes Poconical numerical settings and concepts to Joe DiNapoli influence and recommends returning to primary/original material rather than relying on second-hand summaries.

sources.automation_impact: Strongly supports DMA as an entry/exit context component, but the reviewed blog/video description does not expose the fine-grained candle/distance/bar-count machine rule. Keep exact DMA entry/exit mechanics unresolved unless video content or another primary text states them explicitly.
still_unresolved: Exact machine meaning of inside DMA25x5
Exact DMA entry trigger from the 2022 video
Exact DMA exit rule from the 2022 video

sources.title: FX MAは偉大上位が下位を支配する【ポコニカル勉強会㉜】

claims.claim: The author says scenario construction should actively use moving averages and that meaningful MA overlap is part of what she watches.
The author explicitly applies 200MA/600MA on higher timeframes and, in the H1 example, treats the 200-to-600 region as a possible upper/lower range framework.
The 200/600 concept is described as fractal so the same way of thinking can be applied on different scales/timeframes.

sources.automation_impact: Supports higher-timeframe MA context and multi-timeframe/fractal interpretation. It does not establish a universal 200/600 distance threshold or make the 200/600 pattern mandatory in every Poconical setup.
still_unresolved: Exact timeframe-selection rule for applying the fractal pattern

sources.title: ライン抜けても時間足を変えれば効いてるよ【ポコニカル】

claims.claim: The worked examples explicitly perform H1 environment recognition before M5 execution and later inspect the same structure on M15.

A structure that looks like a distorted head-and-shoulders on M5 is described as a level-topped head-and-shoulders on M15, demonstrating that formation interpretation changes with timeframe while the context can remain usable.
Examples combine support/resistance, right-shoulder Fibonacci reaction, MA context and candle confirmation; one example waits for a bearish candle after rejecting entry on a doji-like candle.
The author explicitly says learning to see MA triangular consolidation is important/needed for Poconical in this 2020 material.
Example exits use FE levels and nearby lows, with exit aggressiveness adjusted after an earlier stop-out rather than presented as one universal fixed target.

sources.automation_impact: Further rejects single-timeframe formation-only automation. Multi-timeframe context is official, but exact cross-timeframe equivalence, FR thresholds and exit allocation remain example/discretion based.
still_unresolved: Machine equivalence between M5 and M15 formations
Universal FE allocation or exit target

sources.title: トレンドライン3-3でポコニカル

claims.claim: The examples start from higher-timeframe environment, then use M5 execution with Fibonacci, MA, zones/lines, right-shoulder formation and explicit stop/target anchors.

For the trendline example, the author combines two trendline third-point concepts, reverse FR38.2, overlapping lines, MA triangular consolidation and a head-and-shoulders right-shoulder entry; the stop is the left shoulder.
The author explicitly defines the immediate 'room' concept in the example as the distance to a lower line and checks whether the planned exit point can fit inside that open space before entry.
If an MA obstacle lies before a nominal FE target, the example exits before that MA rather than mechanically holding for the farther FE level.

The author says the illustrated lower-timeframe/range context is not a particularly good point and recommends using this type on a larger timeframe, again making environment quality part of the decision.

sources.automation_impact: This materially strengthens `has_room` and `ma_path_clear`: room means open price space toward the trade objective, and the intended target should fit before the next relevant obstacle. The source still supplies no universal pip/ATR minimum and no machine algorithm for choosing the relevant line/MA obstacle.
still_unresolved: Which line/MA is the canonical nearest obstacle in every setup

sources.title: FX高勝率な200600MAパターン！チェックポイント追加【ポコニカル勉強会㊼】

claims.claim: The article explicitly says upper-timeframe circumstances should be connected to lower-timeframe environment to narrow the entry point.
The 200/600 discussion emphasizes MA ordering/Granville, stable market conditions and the timing at which the pattern develops as judgment inputs.

The author proposes ranking trade opportunities using a multi-factor score, listing zones, neck/line structures, Fibonacci, Granville, time of day, 3-3 presence/absence, MA support/resistance, stretched-range context and other factors.
The article deliberately leaves each score and total threshold as placeholders and tells the reader to derive importance from their own historical data.

sources.automation_impact: This is strong primary support for a future calibrated evidence-scoring layer, but it explicitly does NOT provide canonical weights or a universal minimum score. Any scoring model must remain research/user-data calibrated until validated; do not invent weights from the article.
still_unresolved: Official numeric weight for each factor

sources.title: FX 1時間のMAとレートの位置関係でロジックを選ぶ【ポコニカル勉強会58】

claims.claim: The author explicitly says the relationship between H1 moving averages and price determines which logic/setup to use.

MA sandwich / dirty MA ordering is described as a no-touch or low-value context until direction appears, while examples also note when all MAs are above price and therefore not obstructing the short path.
If the expected 200/600 pattern does not appear, the article says that pattern cannot be traded; another recognized pattern may be considered, and simply skipping is explicitly acceptable.
An example combines FR, 200MA, zone and a prior W-top neck as a resistance cluster, then changes the expected target/logic based on the MA-price context.

In one short example the author says the trade should be exited no later than a confirmed upward break of DMA3-3; this is an example-specific exit cap, not stated as a universal rule for every Poconical trade.

sources.automation_impact: Strongly supports `ma_path_clear` and environment-dependent logic selection. It also supports explicit SKIP when the expected pattern is absent. Exact MA-sand distance, obstacle tolerance and setup decision tree remain non-numeric/discretionary.
still_unresolved: Universal status of DMA3-3 exit versus example-specific use

supplemental_official_video_metadata.title: FXずらした移動平均線活用術DMA3×3【まとめ】
claims: DMA3-3 is described as supporting/wrapping a trend
DMA3-3 is described as helping indicate entry timing
DMA3-3 is described as signaling a corrective phase and return to trend
supplemental_official_video_metadata.automation_impact: Reinforces the semantic role of DMA3-3 but does not override the separate 2021 official supplement stating that 3-3 can be omitted/preference-based. Keep mandatory-vs-optional chronology explicit.

cross_source_conclusions.has_room_semantics_strengthened: Check open price space to the next relevant line/obstacle and whether the intended target fits inside that space.
cross_source_conclusions.ma_path_clear_semantics_strengthened: MA support/resistance and MA-sand/dirty ordering can obstruct or downgrade a setup; exits may be taken before an MA obstacle.

production_policy: No new universal numeric READY/TRIGGER threshold is justified. The strongest new production-facing semantic clarification is for `has_room` and `ma_path_clear`, but both still require manual/research classification until obstacle selection and minimum-room tolerance are explicitly validated.
